subject: science
title: Where Can It Live?
about: Comparing places: a living thing can only live where its needs are met, so a whale cannot live in a lake and a pine tree cannot grow in a desert (LS.1.1.2). Also living versus nonliving.
tip: Play 'could it live here?' on a walk: could a fish live in this tree? could a polar bear live in our yard? Ask why not.

cards.note: A lake is too small for a whale. It needs the big ocean.

cards.q: What kind of place does a polar bear need?
cards.note: A polar bear has thick fur and fat to stay warm on the ice and snow.

cards.q: A desert is too dry for which one?
cards.note: A pine tree needs more water than a desert has. A cactus and a lizard can live where it is dry.

cards.q: A land of ice and snow is too cold for which one?
cards.note: A snake needs warm sun to warm up its body.

cards.q: Where can a living thing live?
cards.note: Needs are water, air, food or light, shelter and space.
Living things grow and need water, air and food or light.
A rock does not grow and does not need water, air or food.
Water gives a fish everything it needs.
A cactus keeps water inside, so it can live where it is dry.
A camel can go many days without a drink.

cards.q: A forest gives a squirrel nuts to eat and trees for what?
cards.note: A squirrel makes its nest high in a tree.

cards.q: Where does a fish get the air it needs?
cards.note: A fish's gills take what it needs from the water.

cards.q: Which animal can live where it is icy and cold?
cards.note: A penguin has thick feathers and fat to keep warm.

cards.q: What is missing for a plant in a dark cave?
cards.note: Plants need light to make their food.
Soil is damp and dark, just what a worm needs.
